newsletter.title: This week in clones: Creative suites get cloned, and the hype keeps climbing
newsletter.intro: This week saw a wide spread of clones, from AI video studios to full office and photo suites. Several projects are now rated Loved by both X and GitHub, while a larger group of new announcements sits at Hyped, unproven until more people weigh in.
newsletter.outro: Next week we will see whether the Hyped, unproven projects hold up once more people have tried them.

items.name: Open-Generative-AI
items.blurb: Open-Generative-AI, a clone of OpenAI Sora, is rated Loved with 45 likes across 4 posts and 31900 stars on GitHub. It is pitched as a free AI video studio with 600+ models and no subscription.

items.name: CCleaner, CleanMyMac clone
items.blurb: The CCleaner, CleanMyMac clone is rated Hyped, unproven on 430 likes from a single post. It is a free, open-source Mac and Windows cleaner built by reverse-engineering the two apps with Claude.

items.name: WordCraft
items.blurb: WordCraft, a clone of Microsoft Word, is rated Loved with 86 likes across 4 posts and 16768 stars on GitHub. It is a clean-room open-source reimplementation written in pure Rust.

items.name: Content Studio
items.blurb: Content Studio, a clone of Canva, is rated Hyped, unproven on 242 likes from one post. It is an open-source Slack design agent that makes on-brand videos, graphics, and decks.

items.name: PhotoCraft
items.blurb: PhotoCraft, a clone of Adobe Photoshop, is rated Loved with 210 likes across 30 posts and 75319 stars on GitHub. It is an open-source project by storytold that reproduces the look and features of Photoshop and Illustrator.

items.name: Revideo
items.blurb: Revideo moved from Loved to Hyped, unproven this week. It is a free open-source alternative to the paid Revid content creation tool, and it drew 87 likes from one post.

items.name: ArtCraft
items.blurb: ArtCraft is rated Loved with 1565 likes across 39 posts and 37889 stars on GitHub. It is a vibe-coded set of open-source Rust replacements for seven of Adobe's apps, making it the most-discussed project of the week.

items.name: e2e
items.blurb: The e2e project is rated Loved with 205 likes from one post and 12360 stars on GitHub. The author says 21 parallel Claude agents reverse engineered an unnamed product, and the result was released as free open-source code.

items.name: BimCraft
items.blurb: BimCraft, a clone of Revit, moved from Mixed to Hyped, unproven. It is a free, open-source, vibe-coded alpha BIM authoring app that uses IFC as its native format.

items.name: Higgsfield clone
items.blurb: The Higgsfield clone is rated Hyped, unproven on 50 likes from one post. The author reverse engineered the Higgsfield app, including its Genjutsu feature, and offers a version about 30% cheaper on average.

items.name: Discord clone
items.blurb: The Discord clone is rated Hyped, unproven on 89 likes from one post. The author announced an open-source alternative to Discord with limited invite slots.

items.name: subvox

results.text:
Show HN: BBRouter – Ben Eater's 8-bit computer, simulated on 3D breadboards
Hi HN, I kept wiring Ben Eater's 8-bit computer wrong, so I built a realistic virtual breadboard editor. Some of the nice features are side-by-side diff, scope, schematics auto-sync, auto-router (BBRouter stands for breadboard router), and my favorites: upload from the real Arduino IDE and connect to your AI with MCP, let Claude & co build it or help you troubleshoot. The link is the SAP-1 running. You can orbit it, probe a hole with the scope, slow the clock down, play with the virtual displays for debugging, then you can actually build it following the step-by-step instructions. A side-goal is to create a community, there are quite a lot of simulators out there but mostly offline / too abstract to realistically use it for a real build. I also never found one that had a decent UI/UX and worked well on mobile or with a trackpad. Happy to answer anything, and tell me what breaks. p.s. Maker plan is $7/month; code HACKERNEWS makes the first month free and then $5/month for as long as you keep it.
https://bbrouter.com/bbrouter/ben-eater-sap-1

Hi HN, I really like Manim, but when I tried to use it to make interactive small demos on the web, I found that no project can simultaneously satisfy running original manim python code without carrying the bulky pyodide which makes it impossible to embed. So I made one. My idea is to rewrite a js library that is almost completely identical to manim, and then patch rapydscript-ng to translate the original code to js, and support numpy syntax. Show HN: OpenArcanum – An End-to-End Encrypted Alternative to Discord
A while back I recall being told it can't be done and won't be "Discord". To that, I have to admit, it's not Discord. It isn't designed in a way to profile it's users and it respects privacy. There is still much work to do on this project, but it's in open beta with a web client so people can see how it works before committing to a desktop app download. Mobile apps will come later, if there is proven interest in this platform. I don't care to monitize it. The only thing users will ever see is a non-intrusive "Please donate" badge at most, with the intentions to just keep the maintainer nodes and some official relays running. There are no accounts. There is no way for me to see the messages. It is a platform that respects the user's privacy and asks nothing of it's user's. results.text:
Show HN: Similarity, a spiritual successor to 2000s-era OkCupid
This is a side project I've been working on on-and-off (mostly off) since the 1990s. I guess you would call it an experimental "dating site" though it's designed to be fun/interesting to people who aren't single (like me). You don't need to sign in to see how it works, so try it out. There is no swiping. The original inspiration was a 90s-era website called moviecritic.com that let you rate movies and get movie suggestions via collaborative filtering. I thought "hey, what about just matching me to the _people_ with the same taste instead?" And why just movies? The closest thing to this was 2000s-era OkCupid, before it was Tinderized. I want to capture its appeal, while making something novel. Similarity is not vibe coded, though I lean pretty heavily on codex (mostly the $20/mo plan - not a lot of tokens burnt here). The stack is java, guice/gwizard, elastic beanstalk, postgres (neon), react, jotai, and few cloudflare doodads. The match engine is a custom in-memory structure; getting the LLM to load test and optimize it was really a wow moment. Everything is PaaS and designed to scale by itself, cheaply, hands-off. I'm working on some ideas to help with the chicken/egg problem but for now I have low expectations. It's cheap to run and I have a day job. Would love feedback!
https://similarity.com

results.text:
Show HN: Balk – A Baseball Game
Balk is a baseball game. Things like MLB Showdown and other baseball games captured my attention growing up, but never really filled the void of a game. They were fun to look at and scheme, but the game itself was missing something. I think baseball lends itself really well to game design. There are a lot of games that exist inside the game of baseball. It’s a deeply flawed and broken sport, but so are humans, and in some ways that makes baseball better. It’s baseball. You already know the rules, and that’s the point. You play against another person, or against Tin Pete, the bot. A game takes about 30 minutes, honestly I’m not sure, I can play it fast but I’m using the hotkeys. It’s what I’d consider alpha, and I’m still trying to find what’s fun. It’s been a nice outlet and a break from solving business problems, though the same skill set gets invoked: distill a complex idea down to its most basic implementation. Stack is Java, React, Postgres, on a $5 Digital Ocean instance. I'm sure you can bring it down if you are bored. There’s some slop TOS and privacy policy up. No trackers, nothing sold. Happy to update the intention was that these were easy to understand and I'm not interested in selling your data. If you want to see how it was built, day by day, counted from the repo: https://balk.club/blog/timeline.html
https://balk.club

results.text:
Show HN: Clawdline – Manage Claude Code/Codex sessions across computers
I built Clawdline to manage Claude Code and Codex sessions across multiple computers in one place. It runs on multiple computers (Mac and Linux), and you can see all of your sessions in one list. Each session reports its status (working, completed, or needs attention). You can also manage all your sessions and receive notifications from your phone (web app). Herdr, T3 Code, and Orca already cover a lot of this space, and there’s overlap. When I started building Clawdline, I didn't know about Herdr, T3 Code, or Orca. So I built it to fit my own dev workflow. At first, I used Swift to build a Mac app, but I realized that it wouldn't work if I also wanted to support Linux. So I decided to rewrite it in Go. Now it can support both of them. Main Features: - Cross Machine Agent Communication: You can ask a root session ("Local") on your Mac to start a new session ("Remote") on a remote Linux machine. Once the remote session finishes its work, it notifies the root ("Local") session. - Cross Agent Communication: You can use one root session to create tasks need multiple agents. They can communicate with each other through clawdline - Scheduled Task with Webhook: You can create scheduled tasks and combine them with your service (use webhooks to trigger new agent sessions) - Board System: tasks control for Feature, Issue, Epic, Refactor, Plan - Snippet/Playbook: If there are commands you use them very often, snippet can help you - TODO: lightweight tasks - Note: Agents can leave notes to you if they need your attention - Agent Squad: assign role to any task or session - Archive: you can archive sessions and see it in one place - Others: Intelligence session naming, Image/Video display, Voice input, Machine monitor, Usage Monitor, Dev Stack Run, Deploy progress monitor... This project is open source and I have used Claude & Codex to do independent reviews on Clawdline, Herdr, T3 and Orca. (you ca

Exports and generates images and video

No Illustrator vector tools mentioned
Ships only as a generative AI workflow, not a general creative suite
Reported bugs with export, TGA export and pressure sensitivity

Show HN: BBRouter – Ben Eater's 8-bit computer, simulated on 3D breadboards
Hi HN, I kept wiring Ben Eater's 8-bit computer wrong, so I built a realistic virtual breadboard editor. Some of the nice features are side-by-side diff, scope, schematics auto-sync, auto-router (BBRouter stands for breadboard router), and my favorites: upload from the real Arduino IDE and connect to your AI with MCP, let Claude & co build it or help you troubleshoot. The link is the SAP-1 running. You can orbit it, probe a hole with the scope, slow the clock down, play with the virtual displays for debugging, then you can actually build it following the step-by-step instructions. A side-goal is to create a community, there are quite a lot of simulators out there but mostly offline / too abstract to realistically use it for a real build. I also never found one that had a decent UI/UX and worked well on mobile or with a trackpad. Happy to answer anything, and tell me what breaks. p.s. Maker plan is $7/month; code HACKERNEWS makes the first month free and then $5/month for as long as you keep it.
https://bbrouter.com/bbrouter/ben-eater-sap-1

Show HN: Similarity, a spiritual successor to 2000s-era OkCupid
This is a side project I've been working on on-and-off (mostly off) since the 1990s. I guess you would call it an experimental "dating site" though it's designed to be fun/interesting to people who aren't single (like me). You don't need to sign in to see how it works, so try it out. There is no swiping. The original inspiration was a 90s-era website called moviecritic.com that let you rate movies and get movie suggestions via collaborative filtering. I thought "hey, what about just matching me to the _people_ with the same taste instead?" And why just movies? The closest thing to this was 2000s-era OkCupid, before it was Tinderized. I want to capture its appeal, while making something novel. Similarity is not vibe coded, though I lean pretty heavily on codex (mostly the $20/mo plan - not a lot of tokens burnt here). The stack is java, guice/gwizard, elastic beanstalk, postgres (neon), react, jotai, and few cloudflare doodads. The match engine is a custom in-memory structure; getting the LLM to load test and optimize it was really a wow moment. Everything is PaaS and designed to scale by itself, cheaply, hands-off. I'm working on some ideas to help with the chicken/egg problem but for now I have low expectations. It's cheap to run and I have a day job. Would love feedback!
https://similarity.com

Show HN: Balk – A Baseball Game
Balk is a baseball game. Things like MLB Showdown and other baseball games captured my attention growing up, but never really filled the void of a game. They were fun to look at and scheme, but the game itself was missing something. I think baseball lends itself really well to game design. There are a lot of games that exist inside the game of baseball. It’s a deeply flawed and broken sport, but so are humans, and in some ways that makes baseball better. It’s baseball. You already know the rules, and that’s the point. You play against another person, or against Tin Pete, the bot. A game takes about 30 minutes, honestly I’m not sure, I can play it fast but I’m using the hotkeys. It’s what I’d consider alpha, and I’m still trying to find what’s fun. It’s been a nice outlet and a break from solving business problems, though the same skill set gets invoked: distill a complex idea down to its most basic implementation. Stack is Java, React, Postgres, on a $5 Digital Ocean instance. I'm sure you can bring it down if you are bored. There’s some slop TOS and privacy policy up. No trackers, nothing sold. Happy to update the intention was that these were easy to understand and I'm not interested in selling your data. If you want to see how it was built, day by day, counted from the repo: https://balk.club/blog/timeline.html
https://balk.club
